input: Learn to fold a fitted sheet properly

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether they are learning alone at home or need to teach others changes whether the plan should focus on self-practice or demonstration steps.
Knowing if this is for themselves or to teach a partner, family member, or housemate affects how the instructions should be structured and communicated.
The size of the sheet (twin, queen, king) affects the physical technique, especially how corners are managed and how much space is needed.
Some people prefer video walkthroughs, step-by-step written guides, or in-person practice — the learning format drastically changes the recommended resources.
They may only want to master one reliable method, or they may want to compare multiple folding techniques (e.g., on a bed vs. flat surface vs. in the air).
What 'done well' looks like varies — a flat, compact rectangle for a linen closet is different from a quick casual fold for everyday use.
Whether they plan to practice right now with a sheet in hand, or just want to study the technique first, determines whether the plan should start with resources or immediate hands-on steps.

gold.taskTitle: Learn to fold a fitted sheet properly
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to learn the correct technique for folding a fitted sheet neatly, likely to improve linen storage.

questions.title: Are you folding alone or showing someone else how?
questions.description: Determines whether the plan is for solo self-learning or structured to help the user teach or guide another person simultaneously.

questions.title: What size sheet are you working with?
questions.description: Sheet size (twin, queen, king, etc.) affects corner-nesting technique and how much floor or bed space is needed during folding.

questions.title: Do you prefer video tutorials or written step-by-step instructions?
questions.description: Learning format preference determines which resources to recommend — curated videos, illustrated guides, or annotated photo steps.

questions.title: Do you want one reliable method or to compare several techniques?
questions.description: Scope of learning — mastering a single go-to fold versus surveying multiple approaches (on a bed, flat surface, or freehand in the air).

questions.title: Where will you practice — on a bed, table, or open floor?
questions.description: The available surface changes which technique is most practical and what spatial steps to include in the plan.

questions.title: What does a successful fold look like to you?
questions.description: Success criteria vary: a tight flat rectangle for a tidy linen closet, a compact bundle for small storage, or simply 'less chaotic than before.'

questions.title: Do you have a sheet ready to practice with right now?
questions.description: Determines whether the immediate next action is hands-on practice or studying the technique first — shaping the order of the plan's steps.
